title: Comprehensive Test: Concurrency & Multitasking Fundamentals (PY_265 to PY_271)

slides.title: Concurrency & Multitasking Review
slides.prompt: This comprehensive test evaluates your knowledge of threading, multiprocessing, synchronization primitives, concurrent.futures executors, process memory models, and asyncio cooperative multitasking.
slides.codeSnippet:
import asyncio
from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor

async def compute():
    loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
    with ProcessPoolExecutor() as pool:
        result = await loop.run_in_executor(pool, pow, 2, 10)
        print(result)

slides.title: CPython GIL Scope
slides.prompt: The GIL in CPython prevents which of the following from executing in parallel?
options: Multiple Python threads running bytecode simultaneously within a single process
Multiple Python OS processes from running simultaneously
C extensions from executing unmanaged machine code
Network sockets receiving data on multiple interfaces
slides.correctAnswer: Multiple Python threads running bytecode simultaneously within a single process

slides.title: Reentrant Lock Advantage
slides.prompt: Why would a developer select `threading.RLock()` over standard `threading.Lock()`?
options: To allow a single thread to acquire the lock multiple times recursively without self-deadlock
To allow multiple processes to share lock state
To eliminate thread context switching overhead
To automatically cancel execution upon thread error
slides.correctAnswer: To allow a single thread to acquire the lock multiple times recursively without self-deadlock
